findings.text: Logic is consistent with controller guard: ready = appAccessReady && checked && isReady; skipped = every other pending desktop session, so allSatisfy in completeDesktopConnections holds and ready apps go through next.complete, others next.skip. Skipped set is recorded (not []), so skipped apps are reminded later via connectionReminderChoices. A ready app still connects.

Not stuck: Skip for now (all unready) -> all skipped -> finishIfResolved returns stage to .choosing (no connected agent); begin() then resets skipped=[] so the user can retry or pick other apps. Slightly misleading label since it lands back on the chooser, and repeating the same selection loops to the same step, but the user can deselect/exit via chooser.

Comment says skipped apps 'stay selected' so workspace reminds. Unlike OnboardingController.skip(), completeDesktopConnections does not clear session selected, which is intended, but prepareDesktopConnection sets selected=false for apps it newly enables, and setupReminderNames also requires isEnabled && selected && visible. A skipped not-installed/newly-enabled app that never connected may therefore not appear in the workspace reminder even though state.skipped records it. Worth a quick manual check; not a regression of this PR's core behavior.

Subtitle still says 'Connect your apps' with accessibility id desktop-onboarding-connection-required, now stale since connection is not required; any UI test keyed on old Continue-disabled behavior is not covered here. Skip-notice Text sits in an HStack with Spacer and may wrap on narrow widths.

Both new tests exercise only OnboardingState (complete/skip/connectionReminderChoices/finishIfResolved), which already worked; they do not touch the view's ready/unready computation or OnboardingController.completeDesktopConnections guard, so the actual change (view logic) is untested. They do document the downstream state contract correctly.

notes: No correctness bug found that would ship a broken or misleading setup. Residual risk is in untested SwiftUI/controller wiring and the reminder-visibility note above.
